top_choice_rationale: Halide perovskites as solar-cell absorbers offer the clearest underlying principle (composition, structure and defect chemistry setting absorption and carrier transport), quantitative certified efficiency gains from a few percent to above 25 percent in about a decade, wide independent reproduction, and a citation that rests on the absorber rather than on unresolved module stability or lead content. The Miyasaka, Snaith and Park trio follows the discovery chain, though the third name is contestable. Targeted protein degradation (P001) is my close second: a genuine new principle with a traceable credit chain, but it merges two lineages and no heterobifunctional degrader is yet approved. Condensates (P004) rank below because in vivo scope is still debated.
